Submitting for the sake of history.

This run tied Trevor Seguin's 5:09 (Twin Galaxies timing). My old notes say this was done 8/8/2005, but I always submit my dates based on the video proof I provide.

EDIT: 8/8/05 was the date Twin Galaxies verified the run after reviewing it for several months. Because I found the actual date I achieved this run I wanted to resubmit to reflect that. I have a copy of the Twin Galaxies submission form with a date of May 12th, 2005.

The run time is also technically 5:05.846 as re-timed by Simplistic despite me submitting it as a 5:06 again. The reason for this is that VCR recording lag.

However, I'm submitting it as a 5:06 because I don't want to rewrite history on the fact that this was counted as a tied world record of 5:09 from start press at Twin Galaxies.

Thanks!

EDIT 2: (5/12/2025)

20th Anniversary of this run. I was re-thinking this. Since my time was re-timed to 5:05.846 then it should be on the SRC board that way instead of 5:06. Scott Kessler's run should also be changed from 5:05 to 5:05.397 on SRC. Both should be changed for accuracy since we know these values.

I was intially worried about "re-writing" history, but the timing scheme simply changed. It's also noted properly on the progression page, so I think this should be reflected to be as accurate as possible on SRC. The date for my 5:05 on the WR progression page ( https://www.speedrun.com/smb1/guides/jdxw8 ) should also be consistent with the other runners and should be changed from March 24th, 2006 to May 12th, 2005.

tldr

Please:

- Accept this run as 5:05.846 on SRC

- Change Scott Kessler's SRC time from 5:05 to 5:05.397

- Change the date on the WR progression page for my 5:05.846 to May 12th, 2005

( https://www.speedrun.com/smb1/guides/jdxw8 )

Thanks,

- AndrewG

I fucked up with timing my splits after 4-2, got distracted and died once. Also I didn't think I'll finish the run at all, so I played very carefully and leisurely, at a very grandmotherly pace. There is a very large room for improvement, though.

Thank you to everyone who has supported me on this very long journey, and I'm super glad I finally achieved sub 5. Huge thanks to paco, leon, aldyn, and so many other people I can't begin to name, thank you to all of you for helping me, giving me advice, and I couldn't have done this without you guys. Yesterday, I got a 5:00.006, and I was extremely upset. It should have been 4:59.889, but I screwed up the axe grab, and I missed sub 5 by one frame. Even though I've been getting a lot of pb's recently, this really upset me, and I really felt like giving up and taking a break. But this just shows you, no matter how down you feel, no matter how much you want to stop, if you continue, you will achieve it. 
5 months ago, when I was just getting into speedrunning, if you told me that I would get a sub 5 in half a year, I would have thought you were crazy. If anyone out there is reading this who wants to get into speedrunning, but thinks it is too hard, that they will never make it, that they don't have what it takes, just know that if I can do it, you can. Practice. Grind. Improve your PB. If you put in effort, you will get it - With speedrunning, it will always pay off. Even if you aren't in winning conditions, use your conditions to win. Thank you everyone, the journey won't stop here.

I use Nestopia UE with "2-in-1 Super Mario Bros - Duck Hunt.nes"; my Nestopia is set to USA/NTSC with NTSC filter and with screen size "2x", the "No Sprite Limit" option is left unchecked, the "Allow up/down left/right simultaneously" option is left unchecked.

I use generic USB controller (SNES shaped), I mapped all buttons as they should and I use NintendoSpy as Input Display with a custom skin. The XML archive within the skin I made doesn't recognize my D-pad as a D-pad but as a Stick instead and that's why when I'm not pressing any button the red circle lights in the center as if it were a stick.

This was a low 4:57 attempt, as indicated by the -7.47 second delay. Basically: I got 1-1 FPG framerule save, lost that timesave in 1-2, got the 4-1 FPG framerule save to back it up, lost that timesave in 4-2, so I entered 8-1 tied with PB. Got standard 8-1 framerule, 540 BBG, and committed to going for 8-3 FPG, but failed the koopa bop necessary to be able to perform Kriller setup, so I entered 8-4 tied with my previous PB. A clean 8-4 as fast as the one in my 4:58.275 allowed this to PB by eight frames.

As silly as this run is (I lost the easy framerules), I feel that this demonstrates that I am definitely capable of low 4:57, possibly even 4:56. Jokes aside, this one took a while to get. Thought I'd get 4:56 very soon after my low 4:57, but that just wasn't the case. Motivation to play Any% ran dry, and I began to spend my time doing other things. I don't know what brought me to start an attempt session today; maybe it was the frame 65 I got yesterday, maybe it was the fast-approaching deadline for FlibidyDibidy's visual leaderboard video, or maybe it was inspiration from Eddie's two low 4:55s. Either way, I sat down, put on some music and commited to an attempt session. Little did I know that I was in for the best attempt session (thus far) of my career.

Three runs to 8-4 on 4:56 pace that day, and so many runs to World 8 I couldn't keep track. The session felt insane, lots of progress being made, and my friends in the speedrunning server keeping me going. Right when I was growing exhausted,  right before I was going to take a break to eat, I pulled this off. Fifth run to 8-4 on 4:56 pace ever, got turnaround walljump but made up for it with a clean turnaround room. Wish the 8-4 were better and I wish I didn't lose 2 frames on axe, but I can't be mad when I managed to pull this off after doing literally no runs in forever.

Never thought I'd get here. If you told me a year ago that I'd have a 4:56, I'd call you a blatant lair. But here we are. Very thankful for all the friends I've made along the way, you all are the reason I keep going. I do plan to go for mid 4:56 at some point, possibly soon, but I do have my eye on other categories at the moment.

question 1: why did you go to the the start of 1-2 right before you reset your emulator? Answer: my input keys are right by my load savestate buttons.  Question 2: Why did you split really fast twice at the end of 1-1, 1-2, and 4-1? 
Answer: I had setup an auto splitter the day before this run and forget I Applied it until 4-2.

 Question 3: Why do you always die in 1-2 before you get a pb?
Answer: I honestly don't know why. It could be because I don't practice 1-2 very much before a session because I'm most likely not going be going for the 1-2 pipejumps.

Question 4: Why do your splits say 5:06.67 But you claim that the actual time of the run is 5:06.944? Answer: I accidentally started livesplit late so the time was about 1 framerule off during the run. I also checked somewes.com to try to find the exact time of the run and I'm pretty sure that 5:06.944 is the exact time.

Ran on MesenRTA (v0.0.6), using the Super Mario Bros. + Duck Hunt game. Autosplit with smb-autosplitter and final time confirmed with https://somewes.com/smb-time/smb1-bowser-beta/.

1-1: Didn't go for the extra frame rule.

1-2: Lost 0.7 to 1.0 seconds compared to my average runs, contemplated reseting.

4-1: Nothing worth mentioning.

4-2: Reasonably good (I've done much worse, and much better), lost ~4 frame rules compared to my gold split. But gained considerably compared to previous "pb" (unfinished run).

8-1: According to plan except for the full stop at the backwards jump around 2:26, could've maybe saved it by doing a perfect flagpole jump instead (but it was a bit hard since the second piranha plant was not despawned).

8-2: OK up until the end, winged koopa didn't suicide so I had to wait - and unfortunately I missed that the time was at 6 due to this. Lost multiple seconds to this.

8-3: Fortunately, due to failure on 8-2 I ended up on a framerule with a pattern I knew (one out of only two). Executed perfectly up until the end, where I unfortunately didn't wait enough for the timer to count down from 3. Lost a bit of time to this.

8-4: Played very safe, and slow, as this was only my second / third time getting here in a speedrun. Got a lucky with good hammer bro and bowser patterns.

This run marks the start of a new era, there are no more framerules left to be saved, so this is now a battle of the remaining 8-4 frames! As much as I've stressed how amazing this run is to me, this is not my end goal, and I will not be stopping here! 4:54.5xx/.4xx will most likely be my next goal for whenever I return to this category, and even after that, I plan to take this category as low as possible. Now, in recording my capture card I've also noticed a tendancy for the audio to gradually desync over time. After returning home from the SoCal Gaming Expo where the annual FlibidyDibidy SMB1 STA and LTA tournaments were held, I decided to keep playing on console to get a better [4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ctz2UXMjOdM&t=295s) Any% time, this time with 1-2G! This was a really solid run, even if I decided to play 8-4 a little safe by not going for fast accel in it, but I knew I could get a .7XX without it which was my main goal. I'm very happy with this time, but who knows, maybe I'll get a low [4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ctz2UXMjOdM&t=295s) in the future or something :3

BET YALL DIDN'T SEE THIS COMING! During the very same stream that I got my [4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iUunDhU2q4&t=295s).780 on console on, I decided to do some low [4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iUunDhU2q4&t=295s) attempts for fun. My expectations were very low since my consistency with TAS 8-2 on console (especially TAS BBG specifically) is very poor. However after just a couple hours of attempts, I managed to somehow hit TAS 8-2 while on pace! This was also the first time I even got past TAS blant during my session so I was completely caught off guard. It gets even better though, as I then managed to completely clutch out 8-3 FPG, and an EXCELLENT 8-4 despite my rough fast accel consistency on controller.

To simply put it, I am completely blown away with this run! To this day I can barely comprehend that I managed to pull it off. I don't think I'm going to go for [4:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iUunDhU2q4&t=294s) attempts on console since my consistency with getting perfect fast accels is still too low for me to consider adding pl8-1 into my runs. Regardless though, I want to thank the SMB1 community for helping me stay motivated and supporting me through everything. I couldn't have done this without y'all! Even if this doesn't seem like the biggest achievement to some people since this technically isn't an Any% PB for me (that still belongs to my [4:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iUunDhU2q4&t=294s).948 I achieved on an emulator), it's still a huge accomplishment for me, and I will always be proud of this run.

Last night I decided to do some mid [4:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNYUuDghHQY&t=296s) NES timing attempts on WiiVC to show that I still can keep up with GTAce's former WR, which also had a mid [4:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNYUuDghHQY&t=296s) NES timing, except this run beat that by 1 frame! This run was retimed to be a [4:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNYUuDghHQY&t=297s).297, which is a [4:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNYUuDghHQY&t=296s).512 in NES timing. The 8-4 in this run wasn't the greatest, which is mostly due to the fact that I got another accidental D+L while trying to enter the pipe in the turnaround room, that and a sloppy water section caused me to lose multiple frames, but I'm still happy I managed to finish the run out! Not only that, but this was also the first run I got past 8-1 on pace during the entire session, so I was shocked i managed to clutch out 8-3 FPG on my first try!

Anyway, I believe this will be my stopping point for doing WiiVC runs, at least for the time being. The controller I'm using just has too many issues, and the input delay is really starting to bother me more and more, and I'd just like to return back to using either a console or emulator.

SUB 5!

Attending the SoCal Retro Gaming Expo in June was one of the greatest experiences of my life. Hanging out with friends, watching the Classic Tetris World Championship, and participating in the Super Mario Bros. events gave me the motivation I needed to hunt for a 4:56 in SMB1 as my final Any% PB. After a week of practice, I began doing attempts, and on June 24th, I entered 8-4 for the fourth time on pace. I nailed forwards wall jump, and I had a decent turnaround room, but my water exit was sloppy. My worst nightmare came true, as I missed out on 4:56 by a single frame: 4:57.011.

This was crushing in the moment, but I quickly realized that it was likely a blessing in disguise. Now, I had the opportunity to go for harder strategies in 8-4 to achieve a more notable last hurrah. I was already pretty good at backwards wall jump from doing 8-4 IL attempts, and Niftski helped me optimize my turnaround room. While I was hoping to score below a 4:56.9, I certainly wasn't expecting to tie the fastest high 4:56 currently on the leaderboard...

I did match in individual practice every IGT from @kosmic's 4:58 tutorial, but, I constantly left 4-2 at 374 instead of 375 (and sometimes 1-1 at 379 instead of 380). So, I think trying this again without the timer, I would fix those two areas for sure to ensure I'm not losing those two frame rules and reset on bad 379s in 1-1.

Thanks to everyone who watched this week! It was a fun challenge and I hope to get the real <5 soon.

I got interested in SMB1 Speedrunning around early 2019 when I came across Kosmic's legendary first-ever 4:55 and Bismuth's explanation video on YouTube. I still vividly remember that 4:54 was considered impossible in that video, but 6 years later now, I just managed to do it.
I became the 9th person ever to get 4:54 in Super Mario Bros. Any% Speedrun, and the first Asian player to reach this huge milestone. 
It took me nearly 3300 attempts and over 200 hours of grinding and practice, but it finally happened.

This is most likely to be the last SMB1 Any% PB from me, since I'm not capable of doing lightning 4-2, and a high 4:54 is pretty much the best I can get, and I got it. I might keep playing Any% until the end of 2025, but this definitely marks the end of my 3-year-long journey.

First PB in 5.5 years.

The one before that was 7 years and 3 months ago.

This game has been part of my life on and off for about eight years. I found it on my computer, then eventually convinced my mom to buy me an NES Classic. I played SMB constantly and set a 5:03... 7 years and 3 months ago. I kept playing on my laptop whenever I didn’t have the console.

When I left for college 5.5 years ago, I was alone in my dorm, bored, listening to a calc lecture. So I played. Luckily I recorded, because I PB’d. That was my 5:02 – my first time needing decimals.

Fast forward five years. I’ve left Wisconsin, left Dallas, and now I live in New York City. I still pull up SMB every now and then, but I don’t have the time to grind like I used to. I’ve been away from home for over five years, and never had the chance to PB on my actual NES—the one I got before college.

I came home to Wisconsin for a surprise visit for my mom and spent a few days with her. I had some downtime, so I pulled out the NES and started grinding for my first sub-5. I didn’t get it, and I leave for NYC tomorrow, but I’m really happy this PB happened here, with her. It might sound silly, but it means a lot.

Even if I didn’t hit sub-5 on console this week, I set a new standard. I’ll keep pushing on my laptop while I’m away. This run was a little sloppy, with some easy improvements left. Who knows when it’ll happen :)

IT'S FINALLY OVER! I started playing the game around the middle of 2024, and I was around the high 6 minute mark. My first big accomplishment was beating my brother's 6:32, with a 6:18. I then started to use fire, and got a 5:16, then a 5:08, then a 5:06 (which averge made fun of me for behind my back FUCK YOU AVERGE), then a 5:05. This PB then stood for a whole year, I was grinding for 5:04 or sub 5 in all that time, but I got significantly better. Now I have a 4:54 sum of best, I began my true sub 5 grind 4 days ago. A run to 8-3, my furthest at the time, then a run to 8-4 that died to wj, then a run to water, 2 more died to wj, and then a run that got to the end of water, and I swam too early and got stuck in the wall for a bit. The run ended as a 5:01.121. I had 1 week before school started and I didn't want to alternate between school and runs, so I locked in. Today attempts went bad, but I had seen that people had joined VC. And people wanted to see me sub 5. So I started attempts. 26 minutes later, I got this run.

Because of how tremendously long this grind took, I will be taking a long and deserved break from SMB1 Any%, and I will focus on my other goals for this year. To everyone that supported me throughout this grind (you know who you are!), thank you so much! Ham and cheese sandwich.
